content:
We can be certain that Apple will raise prices when it launches the iPhone 18 Pro next month. When Apple previously raised prices across the board due to rising memory costs, it exempted existing iPhone models at the time, but that was only a temporary reprieve.

However, two sources now indicate that this year's Pro models will start at $1,399 — and I really can't believe even Apple would go that far…

Don't get me wrong: Apple has made it very clear that it really wants to protect its margins, and it's not afraid of big price hikes. For example, the base MacBook Air went from $1,099 to $1,299, a $200 increase. Even the MacBook Neo, which wowed everyone with its surprisingly low $599 starting price, went up by $100.

But a $300 price hike for the iPhone Pro is no joke. Apple has always reserved jumps that large for its more expensive products.

The cheapest model in the lineup with a $300 price increase is the base MacBook Pro, which went from $1,599 to $1,999 — wait, the original text says from $1,699 to $1,999 — a hike of nearly 18%, which is certainly not small. But if the iPhone 18 Pro costs $300 more than its predecessor, that would be a 27% increase.

The most upvoted comment was posted by IndomitableSlake

They'll charge whatever they want, and consumers will keep paying. The housing, auto, and appliance industries have already proven this. Why would this be any different? People will just take on more debt. 120 years of socioeconomic history proves that perpetual debt has absolutely no consequences, so why not borrow even more?

Again, the price hike is not impossible. For example, some MacBook hardware upgrade options have nearly doubled in price, and Apple loves that kind of move. But Tim Cook has hinted on earnings calls that Apple won't do just anything to protect its margins.

Speaking of sales, I think the price increase will put a lot of people off upgrading, especially when it looks like next year's Pro model will be the real major redesign.

Of course, on the flip side, the Apple Upgrade program can help ease some of the pressure. Some might think it's fine to rent an iPhone 18 Pro for a year and then switch again next year to celebrate the 20th anniversary. But for those buying outright, a jump that large will definitely give them pause.

What do you think? Do you think a $300 price hike is reasonable, or do you think even Apple might not dare attempt a 27% increase? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
